title: Bugatti Chiron vs Koenigsegg Jesko: The Difference Nobody Explains

scenes.text: One of these cars has sixteen cylinders, four turbochargers, and weighs about two tons. The other has eight cylinders, two turbochargers, and weighs about thirty percent less. One comes from a brand owned for decades by the biggest carmaker in Europe. The other comes from a man who started a car company at twenty-two. This is the Bugatti Chiron against the Koenigsegg Jesko, and the real difference between them is not the one you think.
scenes.caption: CHIRON vs JESKO

scenes.text: Most comparisons stop at horsepower and top speed. But these two cars were built on opposite ideas about what a hypercar should be. One tries to make extreme speed feel calm and luxurious. The other tries to make every gram and every millisecond count.
scenes.caption: TWO OPPOSITE IDEAS

scenes.text: In this video we go through the engines, the gearboxes, the weight, the aerodynamics, the records, and the people behind them. And at the end, we will show you the one difference that actually decides which car is better for which buyer. Every number is sourced in the description.
scenes.caption: THE ONE DIFFERENCE THAT MATTERS

scenes.text: First twist, before we even start. The Chiron is no longer in production. The last of the five hundred left the factory in May twenty twenty-four. The Jesko arrived later. So this is not a fight between two cars on sale at the same time. It is a fight between two philosophies.
scenes.caption: NOT ON SALE AT THE SAME TIME

scenes.text: Let's start with who built them. Bugatti, as it exists today, was revived by the Volkswagen Group. Ferdinand Piech bought the name in nineteen ninety-eight, and the Veyron and then the Chiron were built in Molsheim, France, with the resources of one of the largest carmakers on earth behind them.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI: THE VW REVIVAL

scenes.text: Koenigsegg is the opposite story. Christian von Koenigsegg founded it in Sweden in nineteen ninety-four, when he was twenty-two years old. The company started in Olofstrom, then moved to Angelholm. After a fire damaged a production building in February twenty-oh-three, Koenigsegg moved onto a former Swedish Air Force airfield.
scenes.caption: KOENIGSEGG: STARTED AT 22

scenes.text: That is why Koenigsegg cars carry a ghost symbol. It was the emblem of the air force squadron that used those hangars, and Koenigsegg adopted it as a tribute. Every Jesko is built in a converted hangar, with that ghost on the car.
scenes.caption: THE GHOST IN THE HANGAR

scenes.text: And the names tell you a lot. The Chiron is named after Louis Chiron, a racing driver from Monaco from Bugatti's golden era. The Jesko is named after Jesko von Koenigsegg, the founder's father. One looks back at a brand's history. The other is a family name.
scenes.caption: TWO NAMES, TWO STORIES

scenes.text: Scale is the twist here. According to Wikipedia's model table, Koenigsegg had built or planned a little over eight hundred cars in total across all its models. Bugatti built five hundred Chirons alone. So a single Bugatti model is close to the size of Koenigsegg's entire history.
scenes.caption: ONE MODEL vs A WHOLE HISTORY

scenes.text: Now the engines. The Chiron uses an eight-liter W16, quad-turbocharged. That means sixteen cylinders arranged like two V8s joined together, with four turbos. The standard car makes one thousand four hundred seventy-nine horsepower and one thousand six hundred newton meters of torque.
scenes.caption: CHIRON: 8.0L W16, 4 TURBOS

scenes.text: The Jesko uses a five-liter twin-turbo V8 with a flat-plane crankshaft. On regular gasoline it makes one thousand two hundred eighty horsepower. On E eighty-five biofuel, it makes one thousand six hundred horsepower, and one thousand five hundred newton meters of torque. It revs to eight thousand five hundred r p m.
scenes.caption: JESKO: 5.0L V8, 1,600 HP ON E85

scenes.text: So here is the first surprise. On the right fuel, the Jesko has more horsepower than the standard Chiron, with half the cylinders and almost three liters less displacement. Even the Chiron Super Sport, at one thousand five hundred seventy-eight horsepower, comes in just below the Jesko on E eighty-five.
scenes.caption: HALF THE CYLINDERS, MORE POWER

scenes.text: But the twist is fuel. That headline number depends on E eighty-five, a fuel blend that is not available at every gas station. On normal gasoline, the Jesko drops to one thousand two hundred eighty horsepower, about two hundred less than the Chiron. So the answer to which car is more powerful depends on where you fill up.
scenes.caption: IT DEPENDS ON THE FUEL

scenes.text: The engines also sound and feel completely different. The Chiron uses a two-stage system. Two turbos work from launch, and the other two join at about three thousand eight hundred r p m, giving peak torque from two thousand to six thousand r p m. It is designed to feel like a wave that never ends.
scenes.caption: CHIRON: A WAVE OF TORQUE

scenes.text: The Jesko is designed to rev. The flat-plane crank is lighter, about five kilograms lighter than the previous Agera crank according to Wikipedia, and The Drive reported the claim that it is the lightest V8 crankshaft in the world. A high redline and a light crank make the engine react faster.
scenes.caption: JESKO: BUILT TO REV

scenes.text: This is where the cars split hardest. The Chiron uses a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox developed with Ricardo. A dual-clutch gearbox pre-selects the next gear, so shifts are fast and smooth. It is strong enough to handle sixteen hundred newton meters, all day.
scenes.caption: CHIRON: 7-SPEED DUAL-CLUTCH

scenes.text: The Jesko uses something Koenigsegg calls the Light Speed Transmission. It has nine forward gears and, as The Drive reported, seven clutches. Instead of only pre-selecting the next gear, it can jump to almost any gear almost instantly, for example straight from seventh to second.
scenes.caption: JESKO: 9 SPEEDS, 7 CLUTCHES

scenes.text: According to Wikipedia, the gearbox weighs about ninety kilograms and shifts in twenty to thirty milliseconds. And the paddles have two levels. A light pull shifts one gear. A hard pull jumps to the best gear for maximum acceleration. Koenigsegg calls it Ultimate Power On Demand.
scenes.caption: ULTIMATE POWER ON DEMAND

scenes.text: Here is the twist. Koenigsegg's previous big car, the Regera, had no traditional gearbox at all. It used a direct drive system with electric motors. Then, for the Jesko, Koenigsegg went the other way and built one of the most complicated gearboxes ever put in a road car. The same company solved the same problem in two opposite ways.
scenes.caption: NO GEARBOX, THEN 9 GEARS

scenes.text: Now weight. Wikipedia lists the Chiron at an estimated one thousand nine hundred ninety-six kilograms. The Jesko Attack is listed at one thousand four hundred twenty kilograms with fluids, and the Jesko Absolut at one thousand three hundred ninety. That is a difference of almost six hundred kilograms, or about one thousand three hundred pounds.
scenes.caption: ~600 KG DIFFERENCE

scenes.text: Why is the Chiron so heavy? Part of it is the engine and the cooling. It has ten radiators. Part of it is all-wheel drive. And part of it is luxury. Bugatti wanted a car that could cross a continent with leather, sound insulation, and air conditioning, at speeds most cars cannot reach at all.
scenes.caption: WHY THE CHIRON IS HEAVY

scenes.text: The Jesko is rear-wheel drive and has active rear-wheel steering as standard. It uses Koenigsegg's Triplex suspension, which adds a third damper to control the car as it squats and dives. And Michelin Pilot Sport Cup two tires are standard, with track-only Cup two R tires as an option.
scenes.caption: REAR DRIVE, REAR STEER

scenes.text: Then there is downforce. The Jesko Attack has a huge rear wing and front splitter. Koenigsegg claims about eight hundred kilograms of downforce at two hundred forty-nine kilometers per hour, one thousand kilograms at two hundred seventy-five, and about one thousand four hundred at top speed. That is the weight of a small car pushing it into the road.
scenes.caption: UP TO 1,400 KG OF DOWNFORCE

scenes.text: The Chiron uses its wing in a different way. In Top Speed mode it hides much of its aero to cut drag, and under hard braking the wing stands up as an air brake. In Bugatti's zero to four hundred to zero test, the wing went to forty-nine degrees and added about nine hundred kilograms of rear downforce while stopping.
scenes.caption: A WING THAT BRAKES

scenes.text: The twist on grip is this. There are actually two Jeskos. The Attack is the downforce car for tracks. The Absolut is the low-drag car for top speed. It replaces the big wing with two rear fins, and its downforce drops to about one hundred fifty kilograms, with a drag coefficient of zero point two seven eight. Koenigsegg built two different answers inside one model name.
scenes.caption: TWO JESKOS IN ONE

scenes.text: Now the question everyone asks. Which one is faster? Let's go through the record history, because it is a story of the two brands taking turns. In twenty seventeen, Bugatti set a zero to four hundred to zero record with the Chiron, at forty-one point nine six seconds, with Juan Pablo Montoya driving.
scenes.caption: 2017: CHIRON, 41.96 S

scenes.text: Weeks later, Koenigsegg answered. Top Gear reported that the Agera RS beat the Chiron's zero to four hundred to zero time by more than five seconds. Then, on the fourth of November twenty seventeen, on a closed stretch of Nevada highway between Las Vegas and Pahrump, the Agera RS averaged two hundred seventy-seven point nine miles per hour in two directions.
scenes.caption: 2017: AGERA RS, 277.9 MPH

scenes.text: Then came Bugatti's response. On the second of August twenty nineteen, at Ehra-Lessien, Andy Wallace drove a pre-production Chiron Super Sport three hundred plus to three hundred four point seven seven three miles per hour. It was the first car of its kind past three hundred.
scenes.caption: 2019: CHIRON, 304.773 MPH

scenes.text: But here is the detail that matters. Bugatti's run was in one direction. Koenigsegg's Nevada record was an average of two runs in opposite directions, which is the traditional way to cancel out wind and slope. So each brand can say it holds a different kind of record, and both are telling the truth.
scenes.caption: ONE WAY vs TWO WAYS

scenes.text: After that, Bugatti's president said the company would stop chasing top speed records. And Koenigsegg's answer was the Jesko Absolut. Its maker estimates about five hundred kilometers per hour, and simulations shared by Koenigsegg put the theoretical figure around three hundred thirty miles per hour.
scenes.caption: JESKO ABSOLUT: 330 MPH IN THEORY

scenes.text: But there is a big twist. As of the reports we found, that top speed has not been proven in a real run. Koenigsegg itself called the three hundred thirty figure a theoretical number, and said finding a road or track long and smooth enough is the hard part. The Absolut's fastest numbers are still on paper.
scenes.caption: STILL ON PAPER

scenes.text: Where the Jesko has proven itself is acceleration. On the twenty-sixth of June twenty twenty-four, at Orebro airport in Sweden, a Jesko Absolut ran zero to four hundred to zero kilometers per hour in twenty-seven point eight three seconds. Then, on the seventh of August twenty twenty-five, it improved to twenty-five point two one seconds.
scenes.caption: 25.21 SECONDS

scenes.text: Compare that with the Chiron's forty-one point nine six seconds in twenty seventeen. The Jesko cut more than sixteen seconds. That is not a small win. And it tells you exactly what each car was optimized for. One for top speed with comfort, the other for violent acceleration with low weight.
scenes.caption: 16 SECONDS FASTER

scenes.text: There is also the racetrack. Wikipedia lists the Jesko Attack at two minutes fifty-six point nine seven seconds at the Gotland Ring in Sweden, and one minute twenty-four point eight six at Laguna Seca. Bugatti never built the standard Chiron for lap records. For corners it created the Pur Sport, about fifty kilograms lighter with a higher redline.
scenes.caption: THE JESKO OWNS THE CORNERS

scenes.text: Now rarity. Bugatti built five hundred Chirons in many versions, from the base car to one-offs. Koenigsegg plans one hundred twenty-five Jeskos, built at about forty to fifty per year, plus a separate run of thirty Sadair's Spear cars. Every Jesko build slot was sold by March twenty nineteen, right after the Geneva reveal.
scenes.caption: 500 vs 125

scenes.text: Price is harder to compare, because Koenigsegg does not quote list prices the way a normal brand does, and options change everything. The Chiron launched at two point four million euros before options. Special Chirons went much higher, like the Super Sport three hundred plus at three point five million euros before tax.
scenes.caption: CHIRON FROM €2.4 MILLION

scenes.text: And the twist is what happened later. A one-off Chiron Profilee sold at auction in Paris in February twenty twenty-three for nine million seven hundred ninety-two thousand five hundred euros, which Hagerty called a record for a new car at auction. Rarity, not speed, set the highest price ever paid for a Chiron.
scenes.caption: RARITY BEAT SPEED

scenes.text: Ownership costs are also different in style. Chiron owner Steve Hamilton reported an annual service of about eleven thousand five hundred dollars, and The Drive listed a replacement engine at about eight hundred fifty-six thousand dollars. A Jesko has a smaller engine and fewer cylinders, but it is built in tiny numbers by a small company, and parts are made in small batches.
scenes.caption: OWNERSHIP IS NOT CHEAP

scenes.text: Here is a difference almost nobody talks about. Time. The Chiron was revealed at the Geneva Motor Show on the first of March twenty sixteen, and the first three customer cars were delivered in March twenty seventeen, about a year later. By then, according to Wikipedia, the first two hundred cars had already been sold.
scenes.caption: CHIRON: REVEAL TO DELIVERY IN 1 YEAR

scenes.text: The Jesko was revealed at Geneva in March twenty nineteen. Koenigsegg showed a pre-series car in July twenty twenty-one, and the first customer car was delivered in June twenty twenty-three. That is more than four years from reveal to the first delivery, in the middle of a pandemic and a global parts shortage.
scenes.caption: JESKO: MORE THAN 4 YEARS

scenes.text: That gap says a lot about the two companies. Bugatti could lean on the testing facilities, suppliers, and engineering teams of a giant group. Koenigsegg develops a huge share of its technology in-house, from the engine to the gearbox, and The Drive reported that the Jesko's crankshaft is milled by a small manufacturer in southern Sweden.
scenes.caption: A GIANT vs A SMALL TEAM

scenes.text: And here is the twist. The slower company built the more radical car. The Light Speed Transmission, the flat-plane crank, and the Triplex suspension are Koenigsegg's own ideas. The Chiron is an evolution of the Veyron's formula, with the same displacement and the same number of turbos, but almost every part redesigned. One brand perfected an idea. The other kept reinventing.
scenes.caption: PERFECT vs REINVENT

scenes.text: Both cars also spawned special versions, and they reveal what each brand values. Bugatti's specials were mostly about design, materials, and stories. The Chiron Noire was a tribute to the nineteen thirty-six Type fifty-seven S C. The Les Legendes du Ciel cars honored early aviators. And the Sport one hundred ten Ans celebrated Bugatti's anniversary.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI: SPECIALS FOR STORIES

scenes.text: Bugatti did build performance specials too. The Pur Sport, sixty cars, was built for handling, with a higher redline of six thousand nine hundred r p m and about fifty kilograms less weight. The Super Sport, eighty cars, had a longer tail and a limit of four hundred forty kilometers per hour.
scenes.caption: PUR SPORT AND SUPER SPORT

scenes.text: Koenigsegg's special Jesko is the Sadair's Spear, limited to thirty cars. It is named after a horse that Jesko von Koenigsegg rode in his final race as a jockey. Wikipedia lists it at up to one thousand six hundred twenty-five horsepower on E eighty-five, and its top speed is lowered to about three hundred sixty kilometers per hour for track work.
scenes.caption: THE SADAIR'S SPEAR

scenes.text: And it was faster on track. Wikipedia says the Sadair's Spear lapped the Gotland Ring one point one seconds quicker than the Jesko Attack. So even Koenigsegg's special edition is defined by a stopwatch, while many of Bugatti's are defined by a color, a material, or a tribute.
scenes.caption: DEFINED BY A STOPWATCH

scenes.text: To understand why speed records matter so much to these two brands, look at what came before. In twenty ten, the Bugatti Veyron Super Sport averaged two hundred sixty-nine point eight six miles per hour at Ehra-Lessien. In twenty fourteen, the Hennessey Venom G T hit two hundred seventy point four nine in one direction at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
scenes.caption: THE RECORDS BEFORE THEM

scenes.text: Then the Agera RS changed the game in Nevada. Top Gear reported that it was a customer car, driven by Koenigsegg test driver Niklas Lilja on an eleven-mile closed stretch of Highway one sixty. One run reached two hundred eighty-four point five five miles per hour. The other, uphill and into a headwind, reached two hundred seventy-one point one nine.
scenes.caption: 284.55 MPH ONE WAY

scenes.text: So when Bugatti came back in twenty nineteen with three hundred four miles per hour, it was answering a challenge from Sweden. And when Koenigsegg built the Jesko Absolut, it was answering that answer. This back and forth pushed both cars further than either brand might have gone alone.
scenes.caption: A RIVALRY THAT PUSHED BOTH

scenes.text: There is one more difference that most comparisons miss, and it is about the companies. In twenty nineteen, Koenigsegg sold a twenty percent stake to the Chinese-backed company NEVS for one hundred seventy-one million dollars. In twenty twenty-one, it bought that stake back. Today the company is again fully independent.
scenes.caption: KOENIGSEGG: INDEPENDENT

scenes.text: Bugatti went the other way. In twenty twenty-one, Volkswagen moved Bugatti into a joint venture with the Croatian electric car maker Rimac. Rimac held fifty-five percent and Porsche forty-five. Then, in September twenty twenty-six, Carscoops reported that a group of investors bought Porsche's stakes, and Mate Rimac became Bugatti's president.
scenes.caption: BUGATTI: NOW RUN BY RIMAC

scenes.text: So the twist is that today, both of these brands are run by a founder figure from a small country. A Swede who started at twenty-two, and a Croatian who founded his own electric car company and now runs the most famous hypercar brand in the world. The Volkswagen era of Bugatti, the era that created the Chiron, is over.
scenes.caption: TWO FOUNDERS, TWO SMALL COUNTRIES

scenes.text: And the next battle has already started. Bugatti's successor, the Tourbillon, uses a naturally aspirated V16 with three electric motors and about one thousand seven hundred seventy-five horsepower. Koenigsegg has said the Absolut is the fastest Koenigsegg it will ever try to make. Both brands are stepping away from the pure top speed war, in different directions.
scenes.caption: THE NEXT ROUND

scenes.text: So what is the difference nobody explains? It is not horsepower, because the winner depends on the fuel. It is not top speed, because the records were set in different ways and the Jesko's highest number is still theoretical.
scenes.caption: NOT HORSEPOWER, NOT SPEED

scenes.text: The real difference is what each car does with its power. The Chiron uses its mass, its all-wheel drive, and its cooling to make extreme speed feel calm. It is a grand tourer that can touch two hundred sixty-one miles per hour in comfort, with a key to unlock it.
scenes.caption: CHIRON: SPEED MADE CALM

scenes.text: The Jesko uses its lightness, its gearbox, and its downforce to make every input feel immediate. It is a car that wants a racetrack or a runway, and it proved it by cutting more than sixteen seconds from the Chiron's zero to four hundred to zero time.
scenes.caption: JESKO: SPEED MADE VIOLENT

scenes.text: So if you wanted the most refined way to travel at a speed almost no one else can reach, the Chiron is the answer. If you wanted the most extreme driving machine with a license plate, the Jesko is the answer. They are both hypercars. They are not trying to win the same test.
scenes.caption: THEY ARE NOT TAKING THE SAME TEST

scenes.text: Tell us in the comments which one you would pick, and why. And watch the other videos in this Chiron series, where we look at two little-known facts about the car, what it really costs to own one, and the full story of how it was made.
scenes.caption: WHICH ONE WOULD YOU PICK?

scenes.text: If you are shopping for something more practical, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality for more stories about the machines people really talk about.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
